notes.title: Bloodline Update
notes.content:
Hello, mortals!

A new warrior has been unleashed from hell! 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/69ec53bb87eff946bdfd6f1da36d7dc2aca30feb.png
Val the Darkseed has a complicated origin. In the countless experiments done by Mephistopheles to create a clone of the dethroned King of Hell, only one succeeded the horrid experiment, creating the "perfect warrior".

Bequeathed with Hellsbane by Mephistopheles, Val is a ruthless and wild fighter albeit still a newborn. As a melee fighter, Val's combat style revolves around closing gap and execute the enemy with lightning fast speed. 

Val's unique mechanic enables you to dash into an enemy by executing an attack, making it a perfect tool to dispatch with a Hellbreak or just simply slash them to nothingness!
Though compared to Arok, Val isn't the toughest cookie when it comes to tanking damage, so be wary of the unforgiving hell's army!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/a66deabbec8494c78530075b43132c513aee83ba.gif
"except these imps"
 
Here's the patch note for our latest update:

 Added the 4th Warrior: Val, the Darkseed

 Val is a melee warrior who excels in closing gaps to slay enemies. Utilize his lightning flash speed to quickly dispatch any foes that stand before you! His explosive speed, combined with the power of Hellsbane, nothing would be able to stop Val's conquest to escape hell!


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/680dd6b0fd4a0fa7f01dd6f6f4d714d1685f8cb5.png
In addition to that, we're also celebrating Toge's anniversary with our very own publisher sale! Don't forget to check Toge Production's Catalogue and grab those sweet deals!

Yours Truly,
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/713be6d001c5b6bddef3423f9d4bbdc4685c30a1.gif
Hell Renovation Committee

notes.title: Controller and Performance Update!
notes.content:
Greetings, mortals!

Thank you for playing Rising Hell and for all of your feedback! 
Recently, We've come across some various reports regarding issues to game performance and specific controller not being shown in-game.

Our newest update have addressed these issues. As for the specific controller to work, some tweak on your steam settings are needed to be done:

 Go to your Library
 Right click on the game and select Properties
 Open Controller tab
 Change the "Override For Rising Hell" to Disable Steam Input

notes.title: Rising Hell New Update!
notes.content:

Just a few weeks left before Rising Hell is fully released! Have you caught up with the recent comic? In case you haven't seen our previous post, the comic can also be found on our various social media platforms!

Since the full version of Rising Hell will be released soon, we took this chance to look back and improve the game. This is true regarding some of the gauntlet challenges that seem close to impossible to complete. Various tweaks and fixes are deemed necessary so we hope that this will improve the overall feel of the game. Nonetheless, here are the few changes that have been made:

 New languages: French and Spanish (LatAm)
 Rebalanced various talent costs
 Added SFX when displaying pop-up screen
 Improved performance in Rewards menu
 Tweaked credits menu display
 Fixed some delayed SFX
 Fixed a bug where player's rank is not displayed after completing Gauntlet mode
 Fixed a bug with Trickster Mask relic where talents in Trickster's Treasury still have their names and descriptions displayed
 Fixed a bug with Trickster Mask relic where talent names and descriptions are misplaced
 Fixed a bug where player keeps getting increased combo count when Zelos is hitting the monster Guillotine in defensive stance
 Fixed a bug with Shockwrath talent icon
 Fixed a bug with Weekly Dares mode where modifier descriptions in Pause menu are misplaced
 Fixed a bug where Controls settings aren't updated after the Default button is pressed

notes.title: Approaching The Final Gates Of Hell!
notes.content:
Greetings Mortals!

First of all, we would like to apologize for the lack of communications and updates. 2020 was definitely a hell of a ride for a lot of us. Although we had to move around, delay, and push back a lot of updates, we still managed to deliver most of the contents in the roadmap we pushed at the beginning of last year.

But worry not! We are approaching the final gates! We are pushing to deliver the 1.0 release of Rising Hell really soon!

Here are what we are working on right now:

 More contents for 1.0! Including the final boss and endings.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/b724f4e8bafcad772c68a6f266c68f3ac7315506.png
who could it be!?

 Tweaking and improving the balance of Talents, Relics, and Warriors! We want the player to have freedom to explore as many builds as they like.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/b5315014d6ac9cf19e38109ec4db0219679df9e6.png
for a balanced soul economy in hell!

 Overall game polish and bug fix! We are continuously improving the game by squashing bugs and adding more polish.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/24002e91787e3804917ceb23000576df23ad087d.gif

 More languages! We are working with our localization team to deliver more languages for the game, as well as improving existing languages.

 Console ports! More news on this later. 🔥🔥🔥

notes.title: Hell's Redemption update!
notes.content:
Hello, mortals!

The previous update in our public beta branch is now out! Aside from the update included in the last one, we added up to date achievements, and more will come soon.

In case you missed our last announcement, here's some interesting Mode and changes that you can try in our new update.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/62b82f2773084e5be7e5c627276eef588df50eb6.gif
You can now play Conquest with Redemption Mode option. By checking this option you'll get 3 chances (or lives) and continue from your current progress. Keep in mind that your soul and blight gain will be reduced in this mode, and your score won't be listed on the leaderboard.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/f579732b4d6006cb99d02a31ff046ab4ba910cac.gif
Added 2 new challenges in gauntlet mode; Madhell and Deathrush. 

You'll be challenged with various obstacles and hazards in Madhell, but a single mistake is all that it takes to kill you here so tread carefully. 
In Deathrush time is your enemy! Climb your way as fast as possible and fight the archdemon before time runs out, the enemy here will also drop an item to extend your time limit. Be fast and be swift mortals!

Last but not least, bug fixes and more accessible options in the settings are included in this update. See our full list of the patch here:

 Added Achievements for completing Hellrisen, Madhell, and Deathrush missions in Gauntlet Mode
 Added new cinematic intro.
 New challenge : Deathrush. Race against time and slay the Archdemon before the time's out.
 New challenge : Madhell. Survive the torturing chambers of hell. Reach the way out, and become the untouchable.
 New Relic : Oblivion Bracer. Initially gives 200 red souls, start the game with 90% life.
 Added new Vault of Avarice stages.
 Added new difficulty : Redemption Mode: Gives 3 chances of Redemption, 1 is reduced when you die and you'll be resurrected.
 Increased Agony levels to 24.
 Fixed movement glitch on 3rd Archdemon (Dasael)
 Fixed glitch on 3rd Archdemon clone's attack movement.
 Fixed bug on Sydna's explosive spheres when attacking an Archdemon using Satanic weapon.
 Slain Archdemon now drops 100 red souls, while red souls bonus on boss reward screen are now decreased to 100.
 Fixed some bugs on Weekly Dares.
 Fixed bug on the battle against Magog.
 Choosing Re-rise is now also increasing the agony level.
 Added a 'reset to default' in the settings menu


We hope our latest renovation in hell won't make you tremble in fear!

Sincerely,

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/713be6d001c5b6bddef3423f9d4bbdc4685c30a1.gif

Hell Renovation Committee

notes.title: Devlog: Breaking Through Layers of Hell
notes.content:
Hello Mortals,

We are here with something different than usual. Today, we have our Hell Master, Kriswin Yuniar, aka Rising Hell's Game & Art Director, breaking down the design choices of the game universe's environment.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/3b89bb5cab06dc2c5fd85bebca96bb59df065648.jpg

The Game's Premise

Players progress as they go up the platforms, attempting to literally get out of hell. That is the basic explanation of this vertical rogue-lite platformer. The game itself was heavily inspired by Downwell, which is also a vertical platformer.

(Click here to find out about the inspiration for Rising Hell.)

Why go up? This will take us to the game’s version of hell as described by Kriswin. According to him, the universe of Rising Hell mainly refers to the Abrahamic religion’s concept of heaven and hell, hence the appearance of Lucifer, Belial, Beelzebub, and many other demons in it. From there, the concept is modified with other mythologies/beliefs so as to make the lore distinguishable from the existing ones.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/b7c14b5e1fd9922273ff80b6018d16bd9b3016d1.png

In Rising Hell’s version, hell was created from Lucifer’s body, who was defeated alongside his army and shackled with the roots of the Zaqqum tree by the army of heaven.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/c7a152fa0efe6ff478e2ed5f7f357b7cce01d621.png

The concept of hell that was born from within a tree was influenced by Norse mythology’s Yggdrasil (the World Tree), meanwhile, the name “Zaqqum” was adapted from the cursed tree in the Islamic belief.

When you play Rising Hell, you will start from the bottom and then go all the way up. Each time you are progressing to the next level, you will see different environments as well. Let us tell you the uniqueness of each level.

1st Realm: Pit of Torment

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/36bd1ae607861094694e4cf5d2bc7f57bb1b8581.png

Pit of Torment is the place where you begin your journey. This is the place where sinners and rebellious demons are punished. Their souls are fragmented into red and green crystals, which then consumed by other demons in order for them to survive. This is why the monsters in this domain are more savage, and the place itself is designed to look ‘merciless’. Pit of Torment is ruled by Dagon, the False Judge.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/39e12117f595c218d8d135d02b7dacb4f0ce141d.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/d0af4ae7535e5f328a82cef17f1fb5d26e898f45.gif

2nd Realm: Beelzebub’s Lair

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/c08139304965debe0c0274579e81456d1aa33e07.png

The second realm adapts a more gruesome design. This is because the ruler of the place is no other than Beelzebub himself. In Beelzebub’s Lair, the weak are meat, and the strong do eat. Weak demons are bound to perish in the hands of stronger demons. As the place is designed as a colony of insects, the monsters also resemble the entity.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/9b0cf6256a64ffcd87ffc1771f09794050f09c6a.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/60c64fb38717e19c71e9feba26b27afc0e3e48c3.gif

3rd Realm: Citadel of the Faithless

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/7e42017ab0035da6885a1723c05643db176e98e9.png

After you went through the first and the second realm, you will arrive at a more established-looking place. Citadel of the Faithless is where demons build a civilization in hell. It is more or less a city for elite demons. If you’ve reached this level, you can also see it from the behavior of the demons. They have clever moves. It was said that there is a portal inside the citadel which connects to the outside world.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/6a4c338bb70ecd78edba550e64db44cef45cae95.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/da2c9c67b46a3d3cac68cb78b27e354e45ea0844.gif

Is it true that you can get out of hell through that portal? To answer that question, you’re gonna have to find out yourself, of course. 😈

Thank you for reading, and do tell us if you wish to read more devlog in the future!

Yours Truly,
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/713be6d001c5b6bddef3423f9d4bbdc4685c30a1.gif
Hell Renovation Committee

notes.title: Public Beta Update: Weekly Challenges, New Achievements, and Many More
notes.content:
Hello Mortals,

notes.title: Hell Ain't Gonna Raise Itself: Story Behind the Makers of Rising Hell
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/41107c239956d8d3361a874b18bc2716a2d7fcdf.png

After a long wait and improvements here and there, Rising Hell is finally out on Steam Early Access, yay! We are happy to receive so much feedback from all of you.

As much as we’re happy to receive lots of comments about the game, we would also like to introduce the people behind the game, because they deserve to get lots of love as well after their endless days of hard work in these past two years to make their biggest, most ambitious project come true! Let’s get up close and personal with them, shall we?

About Tahoe Games

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/f5ff1f5f0cfd9a3bf7a249ae9692a66e4341e133.jpg

... yes, tahoe (or “tahu”)  means tofu in Indonesia. It also explains Tahoe Games’ logo.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/351be3e37d601e6dbade98ef34b95b1ee9481058.png

Why tahoe? It’s because the studio is located in one of the major tofu producers in East Java⁠—Kediri. It is a small town, and the studio’s vision is to make their hometown known by all people, nationally and globally, through their works.

Tahoe Games was formally established in November 2015, consisted only of 4 members, all related by blood: Robertus (founder & programmer), Hermawan Andika (co-founder and programmer), Utong Akbar (artist), and Rizal Catur (composer). Kriswin Yuniar and Budhi Luhur then came abroad in mid-2016.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/81f5d2f22f914017d4e0fd973c6ee325d551f05c.jpg

The Idea Behind Rising Hell

Rising Hell was born during a local game jam back in 2016. At that time, Kriswin, Budhi, and Robertus wanted to make a game inspired by Downwell. “The game’s gameplay and graphics are simple, but it is really well-designed and left people with a lasting impression,” the team said, “we want our studio to be able to produce games that have all those elements.” Thus, in the initial development of Rising Hell (titled Hellbreaker at that time), the graphics and game mechanics are relatively simple. Plus, as it was planned to be released on mobile, there’s only jumping (yes, no attacking) included in the gameplay. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/88218e924690e114a337432266269fa9bab416ce.jpg
The team during game jam in 2016.

After the 48-hour game jam ended, Rising Hell’s development continues in mid-February, 2017. Three months later, Tahoe Games then started to cooperate with Toge Productions for publishing matters. “Since then, the quality of the game improves considerably compared to the first game jam prototype—not only graphics-wise but also game design and gameplay mechanics-wise,” Kriswin added. They also switched the game engine from Construct 2 to Unity.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/01d7b3f9be6fdf58e51f921c498e4aece73a0fc6.png
In the prototype version, Arok can turn into demon

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/0d7b0eca84b95192d2a2e29657ae5c090563249b.png
Rising Hell September 2017 Build

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/fc38536ac0cb98577856d693ea32bdcfae4b79e8.png
Rising Hell Latest Build (2019)

No Gamedev Experience? They Can Manage!


Could we create something even without experience? It might sound cliché, but with passion and perseverance, the answer is yes!

Rising Hell was created by people who had no background in the game development industry—at all. The only programmer in the team, Robertus, was previously a logistics company employee. He decided to quit his job and pursue his passion to become a game developer. The music composer and sound designer, Budhi, previously worked as a tutor. He chose to work as a sound engineer and composer in project Rising Hell despite never learned how to play any single instrument. He made many mistakes at first, but look (or hear) his gothic metal masterpiece in the game now!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/7f179c4b226e2da60a2373e6bf4e3293223a4fb2.jpg
Budhi during his time as a tutor

Joined in approximately the same time with Budhi, Kriswin was once a convenience store clerk, who also sold chips and other snacks at a bus terminal for a living. Now he is able to channel his inner artist in this project. Lastly, Utong, who helped Kriswin a lot in animating game assets, previously worked as a security guard. All the crew’s past experiences might not be related to game development, yet they are united in their love for video games.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/01d90f0a2a6c8f13ea2b3df28cd1e5cba4ce1d18.jpg
Is it snack time yet?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/cf09ad17c421e7185370d59b2551f908c27c8adc.jpg
Utong’s profile picture as a security guard

Facing, not Escaping the ‘Hell’

“As an indie, of course, Tahoe Games have limited funds,” Robertus said, “aside from keeping project Rising Hell alive, we also have to consider everyone’s welfare, considering 3 out of 5 members already have to provide for their children and wife.” To tackle that issue, members of Tahoe Games also work on game outsourcing projects on a daily basis. It sounds super tiring, I know. However, they don’t want to give up. “We realize that we have to be realistic and continue doing what we need to do to keep the studio running,” Kriswin added. 

There are a lot of challenges while developing Rising Hell. At the beginning of development, Robertus’ dad fell ill. Needing constant care due to chemotherapy treatment, Robertus have to work on the project remotely while taking care of his father for months. Robertus himself suffers from ankylosing spondylitis, a condition of spinal inflammation that could lead to chronic pain and discomfort if he sits down for too long—especially when working on the game.

Another storm came in August 2019. Kriswin heard news that his father, diagnosed with diabetes, was unable to move his legs and requires surgery. He immediately rushed to his father’s hometown, making it his turn to work remotely while caring for a family member.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/105630e7056c10652594b9af3a82523f9e7d5c34.jpg
Kriswin and his father in his hometown

“This condition certainly stresses me out,” Kriswin told us, “but I know the others are having a hard time as well, especially Robertus, who’s always consistent on finishing his work and updating the build every week.” Then, while giving us a smile, he said to us that he feels lucky to be part of a team in which the members are really supportive of each other. “I guess it’s a perk of having a small member. We have a strong sense of kinship here,” he added.

Life Goes On, So Does the Game

The team told us even with all the hardship, positive responses from friends and people on the internet about Rising Hell fueled them to keep going. The fact that Rising Hell is also starting to get recognition from the international game development community, and got to be showcased in events overseas such as Bitsummit 2018 and Busan Indie Connect Festival 2018, boost their morale significantly—not to mention that Goichi Suda (Grasshopper Manufacture Inc.) visited the booth during Bitsummit 2018 and Justin Woodward was super excited with the game when he got to curate it in the MIX Asian Game Showcase 2018.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/cce929614b0c3abf90292aa03d861c9c667895ba.jpg
Rising Hell Showcased at Bitsummit 2018

“I can’t believe it, I was once only selling snacks at a bus terminal, but now I’ve gone to South Korea thanks to Rising Hell!” said Kriswin enthusiastically.

“As what we visioned, we hope that Rising Hell could give an enjoyable gaming experience and loved by people around the world so that everyone would know about our studio here in this small town,” the team wished.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/836ee607f0c9d26a73c1b2f1e68cf6ebafb2f85c.jpg
At Busan Indie Connect Festival 2018!

You can support our dedicated developers by buying the game, or adding it to your wishlist first! Constructive critics and suggestions (you name it) are also highly appreciated for the development of the game until the full release. It would also mean a lot if you could participate in testing out newly-added features through the Public Beta Branch!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/657000/Rising_Hell/

Hope you can enjoy Rising Hell as much as we do!

notes.title: Dash Your Way Out of Hell in Our Latest Update
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35723656/6710b76fdd270f3cac86525f3fe53839fc822a38.png

Hello Mortals!

Working in hell might not be as fun as you imagine. You might picture us torturing poor souls every day while laughing maniacally. But as part of the Hell Renovation Committee, we need to take care of what's doing good and bad in hell constantly.

Even though it's tough, in the end we... ...laugh (not maniacally) seeing you "enjoy" the improvements we did. [strike]You're all a bunch of masochists, aren't you?[/strike]

Here is the list of small (but many) updates that are just in:

 Arok and Zelos can use Dash by default, by pressing the RB/RT Button (XBOX) or Spacebar (Keyboard)
 The Ethereal Cloak relic now allows the user to deal damage while using Dash, but decreases weapon energy capacity
 You can read the Patch Notes in the Patch Notes section in the main menu!
 Arok’s and Zelos’ arm positions are more consistent
 Re-rising does not reset your Relic
 Increased Beelzebub’s overall Health
 Fixed some issues with Chronosphere artifact
 Controller settings are saved between games now
 Fixed Windowed Mode constantly going back to Full Screen
 Killing Ifrit should unlock the achievement now
 Changed background for area “The Nidus”
 Tweaked the area when fighting Hell Commanders in world 1
 When using a Relic which changes the default weapon into an Artifact Weapon, that Artifact Weapon will not be dropped by Artifact Monsters during the run
 Changed the name of Artifact: ‘Rejuvenate’ to ‘Heart of Behemoth’
 Fixed the warrior portrait when going back from leaderboard while selecting warrior
 Choosing Relic while using Keyboard will show Keyboard buttons
 Fixed the Hellbreak counter in Hellrisen
 Fixed save data when graphics are set to Low
 Fixed a lot of other minor bugs
 Fixed some typos


Now go, continue your adventure in hell!

notes.title: First Patch Announcement from the Hell Renovation Committee
notes.content:
Hello Mortals!

How did your adventure to escape the depth of hell go? As part of the Hell Renovation Committee, I’m sure you didn’t get away too far, huahahaha.

Worry not, we won’t hold you back from your adventure, but making the best torturing realms history ever saw is no easy task. We are constantly working on it to make your adventure in hell … better.

That’s why I would like to announce some quick fix we made recently. Remember! This is only a small part of the first renovation! There will be more to come. A whole lot more!


 Fixed an embarrassing typo in the credits, we might live in hell, but we have manners!
 Fixed the sawblades in the Slaughtering Spire
 Fixed the ‘Cycles’ text, the text will not appear on the first cycle
 Fixed the Level bar in Warrior Selection screen
 Corrected the buttons in the controller layout screen
 Fixed Zelos unable to deal damage to Beelzebub in Challenge mode
 Health, Red Souls, and Blight amount are now shown in the Boss Reward screen
 Tweaked how enemies dropped Blight, players will receive Blight more consistently now
 Added more variations to early stages of the Abyssal Stake
 Fixed the Icon to Skip a cutscene
 Fixed the Controller Line image
 Fixed the Back button in the Challenge mode Leaderboard
